transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-07 | Start: 14:30 PT | Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Jordan Kim (CTO - LumenPath), Maya Torres (Lead ML Eng), Sam Rivera (Product), Evan Li (SRE)

Summary (auto): Discussed Redwood quickstart and free credits, clarified Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private options and initial POC scope. Agreed to trial org and benchmark run.

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — Alex from Redwood here, I'm the AE on this account. Quick intros?
[00:10] Jordan: Jordan, CTO at LumenPath. We're evaluating ways to add generative insights to our analytics ui, low latency important.
[00:18] Maya: Maya, ML lead. Focused on prompt stability and integration with our vector db.
[00:25] Sam: Sam on product, mostly roadmap + SLAs.
[00:29] Evan: Evan, SRE, I'll care about VPC and key management.
[00:34] Priya: Priya, Solutions Eng at Redwood, I do benchmarks and on-prem/private setups.
[00:40] Alex: Great. Today we want to make sure you can get to first token quickly with our self-serve API, and also surface the path to Dedicated or Private if you need it.

[02:05] Maya: Quick question — how fast can we get something in dev? We want engineers to try the API within a day.
[02:12] Alex: You can sign up, get free credits — usually first token within minutes. We have SDKs (Node/Python), curl examples. Priya, quick note on trial org?
[02:22] Priya: Yeah, we'll provision a trial org, attach trial credits and a sample policy for rate limits. Devs can call the hosted API; we also give a sandbox model and a couple of recommended open models to start with.

[04:01] Jordan: Our regulatory folks will ask about SOC2 and audit logs — is that on the hosted side or only on Dedicated?
[04:09] Alex: Hosted is SOC2 compliant; we can share the report. For stricter requirements around data residency and network isolation, Dedicated or Private (VPC) is the path.
[04:20] Jordan: And encryption at rest / KMS?
[04:24] Priya: Hosted supports customer-managed keys via KMS integrations for enterprise tiers; Private gives you full control. We'll send the security whitepaper.

[06:40] Sam: Cost — what's the rough delta between running on Hosted versus spinning up Dedicated capacity? We expect steady traffic after POC.
[06:48] Priya: Hosted is usage-based per token; Dedicated is reserved capacity with lower per-token cost but a monthly commit. We usually show customers a 2-3x reduction in unit cost at scale on Dedicated, but it depends on model choice, quantization, and batching.

[09:10] Evan: From SRE side, if we go Dedicated or Private, how does deployment look? Do we manage GPUs or is that managed?
[09:19] Priya: For Dedicated, Redwood manages the GPU fleet for you in a dedicated pool. For Private, you can run an on-prem package or a VPC-hosted control plane with customer-managed compute; we provide deployment manifests and Helm charts. There's some ops work on your side for on-prem.

[11:55] Maya: Latency targets — we want sub-150ms p95 for short generation paths (~64 tokens). Is that realistic on Hosted?
[12:02] Priya: For small models and short sequences, hosted can achieve low latency, but it depends on model family and load. If you need strict SLOs, Dedicated with pinned model variants and reserved slots is the reliable path. We can also enable KV/prefix caching and smart routing to keep p95 down.

[14:30] Jordan: One of our engineers asked about time to first token in CI — e.g., for automated tests do auth tokens and ephemeral keys work?
[14:38] Alex: Yes, you can provision API keys programmatically. For CI we recommend scoped keys and short TTLs. We'll include examples in the quickstart.

[16:00] Sam: How does rate limiting and throttling behave during spikes? We don't want 503s in the UI.
[16:08] Priya: We expose quotas at org and key level and have burst policies. For production critical paths, Dedicated with autoscaling and fallback routing to cheaper variants keeps apps online. Hosted has graceful degradation policies too — timeouts, retries, and auto-fallback to smaller compatible models.

[18:50] Maya: Any gotchas with the SDKs? We use Typescript + Python.
[18:57] Priya: SDKs are mature, but sometimes auto-transcribed docs show old param names; we'll send up-to-date snippets. For streaming in TS we have an examples repo.

[21:30] Jordan: We run an internal vector DB and want embeddings. Does Redwood host embeddings or do we keep vectors in our infra?
[21:38] Alex: You can use our embedding endpoints and bring your own vector DB. Many customers compute embeddings via the API and store them in their DB. For private deployments you can keep embeddings on-prem entirely.

[24:00] Evan: On VPC peering and private networking — how long to set up? We have strict firewall rules.
[24:07] Priya: VPC peering/proxy setup usually takes a few days to a couple of weeks depending on your networking team. We provide a checklist: IP ranges, TLS certs, routing. We'll share that.

[26:10] Maya: For the POC, what does success look like? We'll aim to measure latency, cost per 1k requests, and quality on a representative prompt set.
[26:18] Priya: Exactly — we'll run a 1-hour benchmark with your prompt set, sample traffic pattern, and capture p50/p95/p99 and cost estimates.

[29:05] Jordan: If the POC goes well, timeline to Dedicated?
[29:12] Alex: Typically 4-8 weeks from contract to Dedicated capacity depending on region and GPU availability. For faster path we can do Hosted + reserved burst plan while Dedicated is provisioned.

[31:40] Sam: Any concerns about vendor lock-in? We use multiple clouds and might want to move workloads.
[31:47] Priya: We provide model artifacts and compatibilities; our APIs are standard REST/SDK so moving between hosted and private is straightforward. We also support open model families so you can bring different weights. Lock-in risk is lower compared to proprietary model providers.

[34:10] Jordan: Can you do a short demo of the quickstart flow?
[34:16] Alex: Sure — I won't share my screen on the call transcript, but the flow is: sign up, verify org, create API key, run curl or SDK sample to hit the /v1/generate endpoint. Example snippet: curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate" -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' -d '{"model":"redwood-small", "prompt":"Summarize..."}'
[35:05] Maya: Nice. For our engineers, code samples in repo is helpful.
[35:10] Alex: We'll push a repo link and sandbox credentials.

[36:40] Evan: Anything else on compliance? We need SAML SSO and RBAC for developers.
[36:47] Priya: We support SSO via SAML/OIDC, and RBAC with role scoping for orgs. Audit logs are available for enterprise tiers. We'll include sample SAML metadata.

[38:55] Jordan: Let's recap — trial org + credits, security docs, benchmark, POC kickoff next week.
[39:03] Alex: Yep. Action items: we'll send the onboarding pack and security docs today, Priya will schedule the benchmark and ask for the prompt set, Jordan to share traffic profile.

[40:20] Sam: Thanks — excited to see the numbers.
[40:25] Priya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invites.
[40:30] Alex: Thanks, bye.
